shared_elements: low-relief carving on tall stone pillar/slab
T-shaped or broad-headed pillar top overhanging a narrower shaft
quadruped animal in profile with legs and tail
animals stacked vertically one above another on the shaft
horizontal band of repeated linear/zigzag pattern (A: incised line under head; B: chevron band)
long sinuous/limbed creature in lower field
weathered pale stone set in a dry rubble-wall excavation setting
justification: Both are tall pale stone pillars with an overhanging broad head and shallow, flat-surfaced relief animals arranged in a vertical stack down the shaft, the most specific correspondence being a large quadruped in strict profile occupying the upper shaft with a further creature below it. The biggest difference is density and organisation: B is crowded into clearly demarcated horizontal registers with a chevron band, frontal-headed beasts and birds, whereas A carries only two sparse, faintly modelled figures on a largely blank surface.
